target_profile.system_boundary: Captured HashiCorp raft Go module: core Raft goroutines, configuration, log/snapshot orchestration, FSM dispatch and transport interfaces. Injected storage/FSM/transport implementations retain caller duties; in-repository implementations are not externalized.
ownership: Main loop owns protocol configuration and role-driven dispatch; peer replication workers own RPC progression; runFSM owns application ordering.

activities.purpose: Qualified support for decision formation and legal advancement
activities.realization_summary: Leader dispatch, voter-index aggregation and follower propagation connect stored support to commit decisions.

activities.purpose: Context validity and acquisition, transfer or loss of authority
activities.realization_summary: Election attempts acquire authority; term/lease/role transitions retire tenure state. Verification checks continued authority through a separate callback tally.

activities.purpose: Recovery and resynchronization of eligible participation
activities.realization_summary: Replication falls back to snapshot when retained logs cannot serve nextIndex; install replaces FSM/history context before acknowledging.
Latest configuration controls voters; stable admission serializes changes, while committed membership governs completed removal.
Library runFSM serializes application and restore; caller implements deterministic application semantics.

activities.purpose: History, persistence and reconstruction of support
activities.realization_summary: Library orchestrates persistence, reconstruction and transport; actual storage durability and FSM snapshot data depend on supplied implementations.

activities.purpose: Client contracts, invocation intervals and observed completion
activities.realization_summary: Library exposes asynchronous futures; admission, FSM completion and shutdown have distinct owners.

facts.meaning: Within this commitment object, commitIndex is the largest quorum order statistic accepted so far after reaching startIndex, computed from configured voter match indexes. This is support accounting, not completed FSM application.
facts.validity_context: Current configuration voter map within one tenure; retained voter IDs keep match indexes across setConfiguration.
facts.durability: Volatile aggregation; log and snapshot data supplying matches use injected stores.
facts.recovery: Recreated with zero match indexes at each new tenure; replication reconstructs support.

facts.meaning: A verifyFuture records self plus successful worker notifications against a threshold derived from voter count. When the tally reaches threshold, or any negative notification arrives, the future is queued once for main-loop completion. The tally itself does not encode voter identity or establish continued cluster authority.
facts.validity_context: From registration until result scheduling/cleanup; worker notifications can arise from append, heartbeat or snapshot responses.
facts.recovery: Not restored; callers must issue a new verification after prior operation/tenure ends.
unknowns: A quorum-sized count can contain nonvoter notifications; whether source-authorized histories make its successful consumption unsafe remains to be checked.

formation.explanation: The elected leader stamps and persists commands, then reports its local match and notifies peer replicators. Sender-bounded AppendEntries and snapshot success report matching indexes to a tenure-local commitment object, which includes only latest-configuration voters. Its majority order statistic advances only through the current-term startIndex. A main-loop notification consumes that index, commits membership and enqueues ordered FSM work; follower append handling propagates leader commitment after prefix checks and conflict replacement. runFSM resolves command futures after callbacks, while log dispatch watermarks precede callback completion.

context.explanation: Normal timeout candidacy requires local voter eligibility. Optional pre-vote precedes term persistence, self-vote and requests only to voters. Recipients enforce candidate membership, term, prior vote and last-log freshness; request-specific response channels and majority tally acquire leadership. Transfers catch up a target then send TimeoutNow, whose election bypasses pre-vote/known-leader rejection but still tallies votes. Incoming qualifying terms, higher-term replication replies, lease loss and committed self-removal end a tenure. Old replication callbacks retain old commitment/stepDown objects; cleanup stops workers, fails remaining inflight/verification futures and discards tenure fields. Already queued FSM work can still complete. Network heartbeat fast-path carries no entries or commitment and may run concurrently.

connection.explanation: Persistent vote/term and log freshness constrain subsequent authority acquisition; durable log entries survive tenure loss although their uncommitted futures fail. Each new leader resets volatile match evidence and appends a current-term noop before advancing old-history commitment. Configuration admission waits for both stable membership and current-term commitment, then changes the support electorate; suffix replacement can roll latest membership back. Snapshot capture includes applied history plus committed configuration, and restart/install reconstruct history and membership before participation/catch-up. Verification is a separate authority-support path: its threshold counts voters, but notification registration spans all replicators. That discrepancy is retained without equating callback count with legitimate authority.

open_details: Verification eligibility and callback timing relative to election/lease expiry.

Transport-specific pipeline ordering and error behavior beyond representative dispatch.
core_overview.rationale: Representative formation, authority transition, old-work handling and necessary membership/recovery/application support have been traced. Local discrepancies and deeper variants remain explicitly open.
